title: Influence under a coordinate change
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ have a basis indexed by $\iota$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner product given by expectation under $\pi$. For any natural number $n$, any function $g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and distinct coordinates $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the expectation over $\omega\sim\pi$ of the influence in coordinate $i$ of $g$ with coordinate $j$ fixed to $\omega$ equals the influence in coordinate $i$ of $g$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
A real basis of functions on $\Omega$ indexed by $\iota$ exists, with one basis vector constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
caveat: The statement uses the defined coordinate influence and coordinate-fixing operations; their detailed formulas are not included in the supplied definitions.
